text: Example comment: a genuine comment goes here — your own analysis, a comparison with real literature, or an observation about the paper's structure or argument logic. Every citation must be real and verifiable. For example, a methodological cross-reference might read: this note's use of 'trustworthiness' maps onto the four criteria proposed by Lincoln and Guba (1985, Naturalistic Inquiry, Sage). Always mark this clearly as an addition by the note-taker — the original paper does not argue this.

anchor: When the content is itself comparative
text: Example comment: keep the anchor short and put it on the exact sentence, number or term the comment discusses, not the whole paragraph; only the anchor text is highlighted in Word. Two comments may never share an anchor, and the script refuses it. The anchor must also fall entirely within a single formatting run: either entirely inside one **bold** span, or entirely within plain text with no inline markers. A string straddling a bold/plain boundary won't match a single run, and the script will raise a clear error. Also note: the comment body is plain text, so **bold**, *italic* and ==highlight== markers do not work here; the script strips the marker characters automatically and prints a note in the terminal, keeping the words. Use wording or quotation marks instead when you need emphasis.
